title: Stone Age to Iron Age
intro: Hunter-gatherers, stone circles, bronze tools and hillforts in prehistoric Britain.

questions.prompt: Which famous prehistoric stone circle stands in Wiltshire?
questions.explanation: Stonehenge is a huge prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire.

questions.prompt: Which of these periods came first?
questions.explanation: The Stone Age came first, then the Bronze Age, then the Iron Age, before the Romans arrived.

questions.prompt: Bronze is made by mixing copper with which other metal?
questions.explanation: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. It is harder than copper alone, so it made better tools.

questions.prompt: How did people in the early Stone Age mainly get their food?
questions.explanation: Early Stone Age people were hunter-gatherers who hunted animals and gathered wild plants, nuts and berries.

questions.prompt: Skara Brae is a Stone Age village found in which part of the UK?
questions.explanation: Skara Brae, in Orkney, is a very well-preserved Stone Age village with stone furniture still inside the houses.

questions.prompt: Many Iron Age people in Britain lived in roundhouses.
questions.explanation: Roundhouses had circular walls and cone-shaped thatched roofs, with a fire in the middle.

questions.prompt: In which period were many hillforts built in Britain?
questions.explanation: Hillforts, protected by banks and ditches, were especially common during the Iron Age.

questions.prompt: What did Stone Age people often use flint for?
questions.explanation: Flint can be chipped to give a sharp edge, so it was used for axes, knives, scrapers and arrowheads.

questions.prompt: Stone Age people lived at the same time as the dinosaurs.
questions.explanation: The dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, long before the first people lived.

questions.prompt: The Stone Age is split into Old, Middle and New. What is the New Stone Age also called?
questions.explanation: Neolithic means "New Stone Age". It was the time when people in Britain began to farm.

questions.prompt: What big change in the way people got food began in the Neolithic period in Britain?

options.label: People began buying food in shops
People began growing crops and keeping animals
People began fishing for the first time

questions.explanation: Neolithic people started farming. Growing crops and keeping animals meant they could stay in one place and build homes.

questions.prompt: Why were iron tools easier for many people to get than bronze tools?

options.label: Iron ore was much easier to find than copper and tin
Bronze had not been invented yet
Iron could be picked from trees

questions.explanation: To make bronze you need both copper and tin, which are found in only a few places. Iron ore is found in many places across Britain.

questions.prompt: What helped to protect the people living inside an Iron Age hillfort?

options.label: High banks of earth and deep ditches

questions.explanation: Hillforts were built on high ground and ringed with banks and ditches, which made them hard to attack.

questions.prompt: What was the roof of an Iron Age roundhouse usually made from?

options.label: Thatch made of straw or reeds

questions.explanation: Roundhouses had cone-shaped thatched roofs. Smoke from the fire inside slowly escaped through the thatch.

questions.prompt: Many roundhouse walls were made of woven sticks covered in a mixture of mud and straw. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Wattle is the woven sticks and daub is the sticky mud mixture spread over it. It made strong, warm walls.

questions.prompt: Work on Stonehenge began about how long ago?
questions.explanation: The first stage of Stonehenge was built around 3000 BC, about 5,000 years ago. It was changed and added to over many centuries.

questions.prompt: The smaller 'bluestones' at Stonehenge were brought from which country?
questions.explanation: The bluestones came from the Preseli Hills in Wales, more than 200 kilometres away. Nobody knows exactly how they were moved.

questions.prompt: Stonehenge lines up with the Sun on which special days of the year?

options.label: The first day of each month

questions.explanation: Stonehenge is lined up with the sunrise on midsummer's day and the sunset on midwinter's day.

questions.prompt: What is Cheddar Man?

options.label: A giant carved into a hillside
The skeleton of a man who lived in Britain about 10,000 years ago

questions.explanation: Cheddar Man was found in a cave in Cheddar Gorge, Somerset. He is the oldest almost complete skeleton of a modern human found in Britain.

questions.prompt: Which people from Rome arrived in Britain in AD 43 and brought the Iron Age to an end in much of the land?
questions.explanation: The Romans arrived in AD 43. Much of Britain then became part of the Roman Empire, which is where the Iron Age story ends.

questions.prompt: What did Bronze Age metalworkers use moulds for?

options.label: Shaping hot, liquid metal into tools

questions.explanation: Metalworkers melted copper and tin, then poured the liquid bronze into a mould. When it cooled, it kept the mould's shape.

questions.prompt: What were Neolithic long barrows built for?
questions.explanation: Long barrows are long mounds of earth and stone built over tombs. Many can still be seen in the countryside today.

questions.prompt: What was a quern stone used for?
questions.explanation: Grain was placed on a quern and crushed with another stone to make flour for bread.

questions.prompt: Which famous chalk figure on a hillside in Oxfordshire is thought to be about 3,000 years old?
questions.explanation: The Uffington White Horse was made by cutting trenches and filling them with chalk. It dates from the late Bronze Age or early Iron Age.

questions.prompt: Who were the Druids in Iron Age Britain?
questions.explanation: Druids were important people in Iron Age society. They led religious ceremonies and passed on knowledge by memory, not writing.

questions.prompt: The houses at Skara Brae had furniture made of stone, such as beds and dressers.
questions.explanation: Wood was scarce on Orkney, so the villagers used flat stones to build beds, shelves and dressers that still survive.

questions.prompt: The Iron Age in Britain came before the Bronze Age.
questions.explanation: The order is Stone Age, then Bronze Age, then Iron Age. People learned to make bronze before they learned to work iron.

questions.prompt: Prehistory means the time before people wrote things down.
questions.explanation: Because there are no written records from prehistory, we learn about it from things people left behind, such as tools and buildings.

questions.prompt: The Iron Age began in Britain around 800 BC. Roughly how many years ago is that?
questions.explanation: 800 years before AD 1 plus about 2,000 years since then makes roughly 2,800 years ago.

questions.prompt: Bronze is mostly copper. Out of every 10 parts of bronze, about how many parts are copper?
questions.explanation: Bronze is usually about 9 parts copper to 1 part tin. Adding a little tin makes it much harder than copper alone.
